text: In January 2020 we converged. Forty-eight of us said "the united states-mexico-canada" on 2020-01-29, and forty-two said "united states-mexico-canada agreement" that same day; forty-one of us reached for "the united states-mexico-canada agreement." Clay Higgins was first to the leading phrase, on 2018-10-01. On a single earlier day, 2020-01-09, thirty-eight of us said "war powers resolution" and thirty-five said "the middle east"; Michael T. McCaul had said the first of those first, back on 2013-06-25. The agreement's variants stacked: thirty-four of us said "states-mexico-canada agreement usmca," thirty-three said "united states-mexico-canada agreement usmca," and thirty-three said "canada and mexico." Two dates, two subjects. We record that when we spoke of trade, and when we spoke of the middle east, we did so together, in nearly the same words, on the same days.
